answer: Agents can earn spending authority by locking a scarce, nontransferable bond that is slashed when an independent challenge proves their accounts share one controller. A verifier samples actions across atlas, jade, and umber markets, looking for synchronized behavior, then submits evidence to arbitrators; the bond pays the challenger if upheld. A sybil operator must fund each identity separately and risks losing those deposits, so multiplying accounts becomes costly rather than free.
